- When sentiment is high (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 1–2 weeks.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early 30-day forecasts when sentiment is low or neutral; add 3–7% bias to early forecast points if sentiment <0.2.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast shows strong upward trend, check if recent sentiment is negative; if so, reduce forecast slope by 15–20%.
- Forecast horizon 30d often lags true price by 1–2 days; adjust by adding 0.5–1.5% per day lag for price decline or volatility spike.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “1.0” (strong bullish) followed by price drop, model overreacts; apply 5–10% downward correction after 3 consecutive bullish sentiment days.
